subject: AcmeHealth — Private VPC & air-gapped feasibility / vendor comparison

Subject: AcmeHealth discovery — Private VPC & air-gapped feasibility (post-call recap)

Hi Sanjay / Emily —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

What we heard:
- Primary use: inference for PHI-handling clinical summarization at scale (low-latency, predictable throughput).
- Key requirements: private VPC or on-prem option, customer-managed control plane / KMS integration, and the possibility of a fully air-gapped deployment for some environments.
- Concerns: how Redwood compares to hyperscaler inference endpoints (networking egress, control plane visibility, SLA), and what tests we can run to validate network and air-gap feasibility.

Redwood differentiators we discussed:
- Private control plane option (we can offer either our managed control plane with VPC peering or a customer-hosted control plane for greater isolation).
- Predictable dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools + configurable burst) vs pay-as-you-go hyperscaler endpoints.
- Built-in KV/prefix caching and batching to reduce per-token cost while hitting latency SLOs.

Proposed next steps (suggested owners & timing):
1) Networking checklist + short checklist for your infra team — Camila will send this today (SE).
2) Technical deep-dive on air-gap packaging — Aditya to share a short note and feasibility options by EOD Thu (engineering).
3) Competitive comparison doc vs AWS/GCP endpoints — I’ve attached a short comparison PDF for context.
4) Schedule an on-network test window (egress/firewall rules + latency test) — propose Mon 10/26 or Tue 10/27.

Can you confirm who we should loop in from your infra/security teams for the networking session? Also, are there any contract/procurement constraints we should be aware of now (DocuSign, SSO, SOC 2 paperwork)?

Thanks — happy to iterate.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying items from our side: 
1) For the private control plane — we need to understand if control plane telemetry (metrics/traces) can be routed to our Splunk/Datadog instance without traversing a public internet egress. Is the control plane on our network or do we proxy metrics?
2) Air-gapped: when you say "packaging for air-gap" — can you explain what components still require outbound connectivity (if any) and what an entirely offline install would look like?
3) Procurement: we’ll likely need a standard SOW and an initial pilot PO. Our procurement lead (Tom Li) is copied; Tom — what timing looks feasible on your side?

Emily, I’ll introduce someone from infra if needed — but we can start with your SE checklist.

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: AcmeHealth discovery — Private VPC & air-gapped feasibility (post-call recap)

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks — I’ve attached a short networking checklist (networking-checklist.xlsx) that covers firewall rules, VPC peering vs private link, NAT/egress rules we typically validate, and sample latency tests. Quick answers inline: 

1) Telemetry routing: We support pushing metrics/traces to your monitoring endpoints via private peering. If you use a customer-hosted control plane, metrics remain on your network. For our managed control plane we can configure a secure VPN/peering + VPC endpoints so telemetry does not traverse the open internet.

2) Air-gap packaging: Two options —
  a) Fully offline on-prem bundle: runtime + control plane can be deployed entirely behind your firewall. In this model, we provide an offline installer and pre-signed model artifacts; no outbound connectivity is required after initial validation.
  b) Semi-isolated: runtime on-prem with a minimal outbound channel for signed artifact refreshes (via a proxy) — useful for customers that want regular model updates but still restrict general egress.

3) Tests we recommend for the pilot: connectivity (ICMP/TCP), TLS handshake validation to our private endpoint, a KV cache warm-up test, and a short perf run at target concurrency. We’ll propose a 2-hour test window — Vanessa, I can run this with your team.

I’ll follow up with the checklist and a proposed test script.

Cheers,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai

Attachment: networking-checklist.xlsx

Sanjay / team —

Following up with a short engineering note on air-gapped feasibility (attached as airgap-deployment-note.md). A few engineering constraints / options to call out: 
- Model artifacts: for fully air-gapped installs we will provide pre-quantized/artifact bundles sized for your environment. These are signed and validated locally.
- License & telemetry: licensing checks can be enforced via an internal license server you host; optional heartbeat can be configured to go through a proxy if you want periodic validation without opening full outbound.
- Security: we support HSM integrations for key material and can map KMS calls to your local HSM (KMIP-compatible).
- Rollouts: can be staged using your internal package repo; we’ll provide a rollout tool that works offline.

We should budget a short lab week (3–5 days) to validate the offline installer on a sandbox segment before a pilot. Happy to lead that run with your infra team.

—Aditya
Senior Staff Engineer, Inference Platform | Redwood Inference
